problem: P_scalar_fd: y' = -1e6 (y - cos t), y(0) = 1, span [0, 1], non-autonomous, finite-difference Jacobian and time derivative (V27 runner fixture)
error_definition: E7 error of V27: |y(1) - y_ref| / (atol + rtol |y_ref|) (n = 1), y_ref = nearest double of the closed form; 1 = the tolerance unit

one_step_grid.description: one RODAS5P step of length h from the exact solution at t (tau = its local truncation error against the exact flow) and from the exact solution plus 1e-8 (R(z) = the step's amplification of an initial deviation, z = -1e6 h); tol A says whether the step is accepted at (1e-6, 1e-9); tol loose (rtol = atol = 0.5) accepts every step

hypotheses.statement: the leg after the pilot starts with h0 = H, so RODAS5P takes another step sequence than Rodas5p::solve from t0 with the user's h0
hypotheses.verdict: mechanism confirmed, not specific to the handover: the step sequence decides the end error; Rodas5p::solve alone with h0 = H (no DOPRI5, no pilot) has ratio 31.85 at A; the leg with the user's h0 passes only because it repeats R's sequence shifted by t_D + H

hypotheses.statement: the state handed over (DOPRI5's y_D) carries an error that RODAS5P carries to t1
hypotheses.verdict: refuted as a carried error: R(z) ~ -12.4/z damps the prefix error below 1e-12 within five steps; the state changes the end error only by changing the controller's early proposals and hence the step sequence (A: exact state 31.844, L: 0.99541)

hypotheses.statement: the restart after the pilot discards the controller's proposal
hypotheses.verdict: refuted: one continuing RODAS5P run from (t_D, y_D) with h0 = H fails E7 as well (A 8.1114, L 21.585, S 63.64)

hypotheses.statement: the drivers' central-difference f_t (relative error up to 0.0001139788 at the step starts) causes the error
hypotheses.verdict: refuted: the exact f_t moves no end state by more than 1.321165e-14; the drivers' difference supplied as a callback gives the bits of fd

hypotheses.statement: the finite-difference Jacobian causes the error
hypotheses.verdict: refuted: the exact Jacobian gives the bits of fd in every experiment
refuted: no run uses dense output; every run's last accepted step ends at t1 exactly and the end state is that step's result

hypotheses.statement: the error norm differs between the arms
hypotheses.verdict: refuted: one norm for all arms (V27 E7 definition); in it N's error is far below the tolerance unit 1

hypotheses.statement: RODAS5P's own end error on this problem varies with the step sequence by more than the factor 3 of E7
hypotheses.verdict: confirmed: over h0 = 10^(-6 + j/8), j = 0..40, Rodas5p::solve alone has end errors from 0.02554 to 62.279 times that of h0 = 1e-3 at A; 31 of 41 exceed 3

cause: On P_scalar_fd the end error of every RODAS5P run is the local truncation error of its last step: earlier errors, the DOPRI5 prefix's included, are damped by R(z) ~ -12.4/z (|z| = 1e6 h >= 18 on every step of the route's leg and of R), and the local error of a step of length h on the slow manifold grows like h^3 (one-step grid: slopes 2.9607 to 3.027 for h >= 1e-2; finite-difference derivatives play no part). After its first steps the controller grows each step by its cap 5 because the estimate is far below tolerance, so the last step's length is set by where the ramp from h0 lands before t1, not by the tolerance (the h0 scans at A and L are identical). Rodas5p::solve from t0 with h0 = 1e-3 lands with a short last step (0.219): its error is 0.05692 times the median over h0. The FBP leg, a plain Rodas5p::solve from t_D + H with h0 = H, lands with last steps 0.7433171 (A) and 0.3261414 (L); the same happens without any handover (Rodas5p::solve from t0 with h0 = H: ratio 31.85 at A). E7 failed because its reference R is a lucky step sequence and the rule has no floor; the route has no defect here. Errors in the tolerance unit: N 0.004119489 (A), 2.874489e-07 (L).
